Hodasz Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Hodász, Hungary

Not demolished. Hodász's Jewish cemetery has been in use since at least 1875, the date of its earliest surviving gravestone, and remained active until at least 1951, per its latest known tombstone. The town's Jewish population grew from 192 in 1840 to 236 by 1880 (out of 1,093 residents), with local Jewish families playing a prominent economic role - including a kosher butchery and a livestock trade. By 1944 the Orthodox community numbered 162, with its own rabbi; that year, 40 Jewish families were deported, and most of Hodász's Jews were killed in the Holocaust. The synagogue was demolished in the late 1950s. No Jews live in Hodász today, but the cemetery remains fenced and actively maintained.
